answer.policy_title: Evolent Clinical Guideline for Cervical Spine Surgery (part of the '2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines'); formerly published as the 'National Imaging Associates (NIA) Clinical Guidelines: Cervical Spine Surgery'
answer.effective_date: Original Date: July 2008; Last Revised Date: December 2025; Implementation Date: July 2026; stated coverage period: July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027 (the version that would have been in force for an August 10, 2026 determination)
criteria_quotes: ANTERIOR CERVICAL DISCECTOMY WITH FUSION (ACDF) – SINGLE LEVEL: 'When ALL of the following criteria are met: • Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity • Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment. Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute "inability to complete" treatment. • Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at the level corresponding with the clinical findings.'

Same guideline, exceptions section: ACDF may be approved 'as first-line treatment without conservative care measures' only for: myelopathy with progressive neurologic deficits, progressive neurologic deficit with imaging-confirmed cord/nerve compression, significant cord/nerve root compression from tumor/infection/trauma, or radiographically defined fracture/instability (sagittal angulation >11° or >3.5mm subluxation with cord/radicular dysfunction, or C1 atlantodental interval subluxation >3mm adult/>5mm child).

'Not recommended: In cases of neck pain alone, without neurological deficits, and no evidence of significant spinal nerve root or cord compression on MRI or CT.' (Cross-references a separate 'Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain' section of the same guideline for pure axial-pain presentations.)

An earlier (2024) version of the same NIA/Evolent guideline for this CPT code spelled the conservative-care requirement out more concretely: 'Persistent or recurrent symptoms/pain with functional limitations that are unresponsive to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative treatment... Documented failure of at least 6 consecutive weeks in the last 6 months of any 2 of the following physician-directed conservative treatments: Analgesics, steroids, and/or NSAIDs; Structured program of physical therapy; Structured home exercise program prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider or physician; Epidural steroid injections and/or selective nerve root block.' The patient's file should be checked against whichever exact version/date was cited by the reviewer, since the wording changed somewhat between the 2024 and 2026 editions.
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the August 10, 2026 notice date, i.e., appeal must be RECEIVED by February 6, 2027 (as stated on the denial letter).
answer.submission_route: Dean Health Plan's public Grievance and Appeals page (deancare.com/Legal/Grievances-Appeals) states that for Individual/Marketplace (ACA) plan members, written grievances/appeals must be sent to: Medica – Dean, Route CP595IFB, P.O. Box 9310, Minneapolis, MN 55440-9310; Fax: 952-992-3198. The same page lists a phone line — (608) 828-1991 (TTY 711) — for oral/expedited grievance or appeal requests, and Member Services can also be reached at 1-800-279-1301. NOTE: I could not fully re-load this page live (it returned an access-blocked response on direct fetch, and its content is dated to a 2024 revision cycle per the cached snippet), so the patient should confirm the exact current mailing address/fax and any online portal option either from the appeal-instructions section of the full denial letter itself (which typically restates this) or by calling Dean/Medica Member Services using the number on the back of the ID card before mailing the appeal.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because Dean Health Plan delegates prior-authorization and medical-necessity review for musculoskeletal/spine surgeries (including cervical fusion, CPT 22551) to Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA) under its MSK Management Program, the specific guideline text applied to this member's case can be obtained by: (1) asking Dean/Medica Member Services (number on the denial letter or ID card) for a copy of the exact medical policy/clinical guideline and version/date used in this denial, which they are required to provide on request; (2) asking the treating surgeon's office, since NIA/Evolent typically faxes/sends the applicable clinical guideline and the specific unmet criterion to the ordering provider as part of the review; (3) having the provider or an authorized representative request the guideline through RadMD.com (Evolent's authorization portal, registration required) under 'Clinical Guidelines' > 'Musculoskeletal Surgery (MSK)'; or (4) citing 'Evolent Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery' (or its predecessor number NIA_CG_307) by name when requesting records for the appeal file, and asking Dean to confirm in writing which exact version (effective date) governed this determination.
answer.notes: Dean Health Plan does not appear to publish its own separately authored medical policy specifically for cervical fusion/CPT 22551; publicly available Dean provider-training material confirms that Dean Health Plan's non-emergent inpatient/outpatient cervical and lumbar spine surgery prior authorizations (which explicitly include 'Cervical Anterior Decompression with Fusion – Single & Multiple Levels') are managed by National Imaging Associates (NIA), now operating as Evolent, using Evolent/NIA's clinical guidelines posted on RadMD.com. I located and quoted the current Evolent guideline (Evolent_CG_1759, effective July 2026–July 2027, last revised December 2025) covering CPT 22551 under 'Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Single Level,' which is the guideline that would ordinarily have been applied to a request denied on 2026-08-10. I also located and quoted the 2024 edition of the same guideline (then numbered NIA_CG_307) for comparison, because its conservative-care requirement is spelled out in more concrete, actionable detail (duration, specific modalities, '2-of-4' requirement) than the 2026 edition's more general language. I was not able to directly confirm — because Dean's provider/member web pages returned access-blocked (403) responses to automated fetch — that this exact guideline, rather than some other or updated Dean-specific medical policy, was the document actually cited by the reviewer in this member's case. The patient/provider should ask Dean/Medica explicitly to identify, in writing, the exact policy name, number, and version date relied upon for this specific denial, and should independently verify the appeal mailing address/fax/deadline instructions printed on the full denial letter itself, since only an excerpt of that letter was provided to me.

Purpose This guideline outlines the key surgical treatments and indications for common cervical spinal disorders and is based upon the best available evidence. Spine surgery is a complex area of medicine, and this document breaks out the clinical indications by surgical type. This guideline does not address spinal deformity surgeries or the clinical indications for spinal deformity surgery. Scope Spinal surgeries should be performed only by those with extensive and specialized surgical training (neurosurgery, orthopedic surgery). Choice of surgical approach is based on anatomy, pathology, and the surgeon's experience and preference. Instrumentation, bone formation or grafting materials, including biologics, should be used at the surgeon’s discretion; however, use should be limited to FDA approved indications regarding the specific devices or biologics. Special Note In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery.
